claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First of all, could you please tell me how many children you'd like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17 years old, I need to ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training? This would include things like A-levels, Scottish Highers, T-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar qualifications – but not apprenticeships in England.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He left school and he's working now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. I have a couple more questions about Alex's work situation.

Is Alex working 24 hours or more per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he works full-time at the supermarket.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Unfortunately, based on what you've told me, it appears you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. This is because Alex is over 16, is no longer in approved education or training, and is working 24 hours or more per week.

However, before I make a final determination, I just need to confirm a couple of things about your own circumstances:

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just one more question: Does Alex live with you, or if not, do you contribute towards his upkeep (such as food, clothes, or pocket money) at least the same amount as the Child Benefit rate?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information.

Based on what you've told me, I'm now able to make a determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

- While you meet the basic requirements (you live in the UK and Alex lives with you), the rules for children aged 16 and over apply to Alex.
- For children between 16 and 20, you can normally still qualify for Child Benefit **only if** they remain in approved education or training.
- Since Alex has left school and is working full-time (24+ hours per week), you are not eligible for Child Benefit for him.

**Please note:** If Alex's circumstances change in the future – for example, if he returns to approved education or training – you may be able to claim Child Benefit again at that point.

I'm sorry I couldn't bring you better news. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
